note: XPL2 PC Link input passthrough test vectors (protocol.md section 2.19), generated by docs/gen_input_vectors.py. Coordinates are normalized 0..65535 across the content the phone displays; the server maps them onto its desktop pixels. 'wire' pins each message's newline-JSON encoding; 'mapping' pins the coordinate map in both directions, including a letterboxed frame; 'sessions' drive the policy to the platform-neutral actions it injects, covering the encryption gate, the operator switch, the content drops (a key not in the map, a coordinate out of range), coalescing, sub-pixel accumulation and release-on-teardown. Consumed byte-identically by the Rust, Kotlin and Swift suites.

absolute.name: last pixel, never past the edge

relative.name: a sub-pixel nudge floors to zero

letterbox.name: in the top bar is nowhere
in the bottom bar is nowhere

sessions.name: input on a plaintext session injects nothing
input disabled by the operator injects nothing
a key not in the map is dropped, the rest applied
an out-of-range coordinate is dropped, a valid one applied
an over-cap batch is dropped whole
a mixed batch injects in order, motion coalesced
a slow drag carries its sub-pixel remainder across events
held keys and buttons are released on teardown
